Universal power series of Seleznev with parameters in
several variables
K. Maronikolakis and G. Stamatiou
Abstract
We generalize the universal power series of Seleznev to several variables and
we allow the coeﬃcients to depend on parameters. Then, the approximable func-
tions may depend on the same parameters. The universal approximation holds on
products K =
d
Y
i=1
Ki, where Ki ⊆C are compact sets and C \ Ki are connected,
i = 1, . . . , d and 0 /∈K. On such K the partial sums approximate uniformly any
polynomial. Finally, the partial sums may be replaced by more general expressions.
The phenomenon is topologically and algebraically generic.
AMS classiﬁcation numbers: 30K05, 32A05.
Key words and phrases: Universal Taylor series, Baire’s theorem, generic property,
Mergelyan’s theorem, product of planar sets.

The Algebra AD(L)
In this section we introduce some context from [3] which will be useful later on.
Deﬁnition 2.1. [3] Let L ⊂Cn be a compact set. A function f : L →C is said to belong
to the class AD(L) if it is continuous on L and, for every open disk D ⊂C and every
injective mapping φ : D →L ⊂Cn holomorphic on D, the composition f ◦φ : D →C is
holomorphic on D.
We recall that a function φ : D →Cn, where D is a planar domain, is holomorphic if
each coordinate is a holomorphic function.

Remark. We have proven that, for a ﬁxed enumeration of Nd, the set of formal power
series in H(Ω)ℵ0 having the desired universal approximation property with respect to this
enumeration is a Gδ and dense set. Using Baire’s Theorem, it easily follows that the set of
formal power series in H(Ω)ℵ0 that have the same universal approximation property with
respect to any countable family of enumerations of Nd is a Gδ and dense set. Since the
set of all enumerations of Nd is uncountable, a natural question that arises is whether we
can generalise the result when the formal power series have the universal approximation
property with respect to all enumerations of Nd. The answer to this question is negative.
The proof is similar to a result in Section 6 of [4].
